answer: Each agent identity mints as an NFT bonded into a shallow AMM pool, so trust depth behaves like a narrow jetty: an attacker cloning identities must buy out the bonding curve, paying slippage that scales superlinearly with each new sybil. The cost curve steepens past a canyon of depth, since every additional bonded clone pushes marginal price against the attacker's own capital, making mass identity cheap only until the pool thins. This mechanism caps at a limit: a whale can subsidize depth to harbor thousands of clones, so bonding alone fails without slashing by verifiers.
